questions.question_english: Regarding the institutional architecture of the National Pension System (NPS), which statement precisely describes the nature of a Tier I account?
options_english: A voluntary, flexible savings facility with full tax exemption and unrestricted anytime withdrawal limits for subscribers.
A temporary holding transit account utilized solely to park monthly pension deductions prior to crediting them into the GPF.
A statutory life insurance savings scheme offering guaranteed sovereign returns along with an assured maturity sum.
A mandatory, non-withdrawable individual pension account governed by strict statutory withdrawal and exit restrictions.
questions.explanation_english:
The NPS architecture operates on a distinct two-tier model overseen by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

Key Characteristics of the Tier I Account:
1. Statutory Nature: Under the CCS (Implementation of NPS) Rules, 2021 and PFRDA Regulations, the Tier I account is the core, mandatory individual pension account tied to the Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN). Every government servant entering service on or after 01.01.2004 must be enrolled into Tier I.
2. Non-Withdrawable Corpus: It is designed strictly for retirement wealth creation and is essentially non-withdrawable during active service. Funds accumulated cannot be withdrawn at will like a conventional bank or savings account.
3. Controlled Exit and Withdrawals: Withdrawals prior to superannuation are permissible only under rigid statutory guidelines—namely, partial withdrawals (up to 25% of own contributions after 3 years for specific defined exigencies like illness, child education/marriage, house purchase) up to a maximum of 3 times, or premature exit where 80% must be annuitized.
4. Superannuation Mandate: At superannuation (age 60), a minimum of 40% of the accumulated Tier I corpus must be utilized to purchase an immediate annuity from an approved Annuity Service Provider (ASP), and the remaining balance (up to 60%) can be withdrawn as a lump sum (100% tax-exempt).
questions.explanation_hindi:
NPS की संरचना पेंशन फंड नियामक और विकास प्राधिकरण (PFRDA) द्वारा निर्धारित दो-स्तरीय (Two-tier) मॉडल पर आधारित है।

टियर I खाते की प्रमुख विशेषताएं:
1. अनिवार्य एवं सांविधिक प्रकृति: सीसीएस (NPS का क्रियान्वयन) नियम, 2021 और PFRDA विनियमों के तहत, टियर I खाता स्थायी सेवानिवृत्ति खाता संख्या (PRAN) से जुड़ा मुख्य एवं अनिवार्य पेंशन खाता है। 01.01.2004 को या उसके बाद सेवा में आने वाले प्रत्येक सरकारी कर्मचारी का टियर I खाता होना अनिवार्य है।
2. गैर-निकासी योग्य संचित कोष: यह खाता विशेष रूप से वृद्धावस्था पेंशन सुरक्षा के लिए है और सक्रिय सेवाकाल के दौरान अनिवार्य रूप से गैर-निकासी योग्य (Non-withdrawable) होता है। इसे साधारण बचत खाते की तरह स्वेच्छा से जब चाहें तब नहीं निकाला जा सकता।
3. नियंत्रित निकासी एवं निकास: सेवानिवृत्ति से पहले निकासी केवल सख्त सांविधिक शर्तों के तहत ही अनुमत है—जैसे 3 वर्ष की सेवा के बाद केवल विशिष्ट आवश्यकताओं (बच्चों की उच्च शिक्षा/विवाह, गंभीर बीमारी, मकान निर्माण) के लिए अपने स्वयं के अंशदान का अधिकतम 25% तक (पूरी सेवा में अधिकतम 3 बार)। समयपूर्व निकास पर 80% राशि की वार्षिकी (Annuity) खरीदना अनिवार्य होता है।
4. अधिवर्षिता पर नियम: 60 वर्ष की आयु या सेवानिवृत्ति पर, टियर I कोष का न्यूनतम 40% हिस्सा वार्षिकी खरीदने के लिए उपयोग किया जाना अनिवार्य है तथा शेष 60% एकमुश्त कर-मुक्त निकाला जा सकता है।

questions.question_english: Under the General Provident Fund (Central Services) Rules, 1960, how many times in a single financial year is a subscriber permitted to alter their rate of monthly subscription?
options_english: The monthly subscription rate cannot be altered at all during the financial year once fixed.
It may be reduced once and enhanced twice during a financial year.
The subscription amount can be freely changed every month at the employee's choice.
The subscription amount can strictly be altered only in the month of March each year.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 7(4) of the General Provident Fund (Central Services) Rules, 1960:
1. **Permissible Frequency:** A subscriber may alter their monthly subscription amount during the course of a financial year. Specifically, the rate of subscription may be:
   - **Reduced once** at any time during the financial year, and
   - **Enhanced twice** at any time during the same financial year.
2. **Statutory Limits:**
   - **Minimum:** The subscription shall not be less than 6% of the subscriber's monthly emoluments (basic pay).
   - **Maximum:** The subscription shall not exceed 100% of the subscriber's monthly emoluments. Additionally, under DoP&PW orders issued in 2022, the cumulative annual GPF subscription is capped at ₹5 Lakh per financial year to restrict tax-free interest accrual.
3. **DDO Procedure:** The employee must submit written intimation to the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) in advance of the preparation of the pay bill for the relevant month.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य भविष्य निधि (केंद्रीय सेवाएं) नियम, 1960 के नियम 7(4) के अनुसार:
1. **अंशदान परिवर्तन की अनुमत आवृत्ति:** एक अभिदाता को वित्तीय वर्ष के दौरान अपने मासिक अंशदान में परिवर्तन करने की अनुमति होती है। नियमानुसार, अंशदान की दर को:
   - वित्तीय वर्ष में किसी भी समय **एक बार घटाया (कम किया)** जा सकता है, तथा
   - वित्तीय वर्ष में किसी भी समय **दो बार बढ़ाया** जा सकता है।
2. **वैधानिक सीमाएं:**
   - **न्यूनतम:** कर्मचारी की परिलब्धियों (मूल वेतन) के 6% से कम नहीं हो सकता।
   - **अधिकतम:** कर्मचारी की कुल परिलब्धियों (100%) से अधिक नहीं हो सकता, और DoP&PW के 2022 के निर्देशों के अनुसार प्रति वित्तीय वर्ष कुल GPF अंशदान की अधिकतम सीमा ₹5 लाख निर्धारित की गई है।
3. **DDO की प्रक्रिया:** कर्मचारी को संबंधित माह के वेतन बिल तैयार होने से पूर्व आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को लिखित आवेदन प्रस्तुत करना होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Reduced once and enhanced twice during a financial year.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the General Provident Fund (Central Services) Rules, 1960, a subscriber is permitted to alter their rate of monthly subscription during a financial year. questions.question_english: A Post Graduate Teacher (PGT) covered under the National Pension System (NPS) dies in service. In accordance with service rules and the option exercised, the government sanctions a regular monthly Family Pension under the CCS (Pension) Rules to the eligible spouse. In this scenario, how is the accumulated NPS Tier-I corpus (employee and government contributions with accrued returns) dealt with?
options_english: The employee's accumulated contribution and returns are paid in lump sum to the family, while the government contribution and returns are refunded to the Government
The entire accumulated NPS corpus (both employee and government shares) is paid in full directly to the spouse alongside the monthly family pension
The entire corpus is compulsorily converted into an immediate commercial annuity for the minor children
The entire corpus is permanently surrendered to the government without any lump sum payout to the family
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 10 and Rule 20 of the Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021 (originating from Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare OM dated 05.05.2009), when a Central Government employee covered under NPS dies during service and Family Pension is sanctioned to the eligible family member under the CCS (Pension) Rules or CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules:
1. The Government contribution and the returns accrued thereon in the subscriber's NPS Tier-I account are transferred and refunded to the Government treasury account.
2. The accumulated employee's contribution along with all returns accrued thereon in the PRAN is paid in a lump sum to the nominee / eligible family member.
In addition, the family receives Death Gratuity as per qualifying service. Conversely, if the family opts for benefits under the NPS regulations instead of CCS Family Pension, the entire accumulated pension wealth (both employee and employer contributions) is utilized as per PFRDA exit regulations (annuity plus lump sum).
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली का क्रियान्वयन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 10 और 20 (तथा DoP&PW के दिनांक 05.05.2009 के ऐतिहासिक आदेश) के अनुसार, यदि सेवाकाल के दौरान किसी एनपीएस कर्मचारी की मृत्यु हो जाती है और उसके परिवार को सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के तहत पारिवारिक पेंशन (Family Pension) प्रदान की जाती है, तो:
1. कर्मचारी के PRAN (टियर-I) खाते में जमा सरकारी अंशदान और उस पर अर्जित ब्याज/लाभ की पूरी राशि सरकारी खाते (सरकारी खजाने) में वापस (refund) जमा करा दी जाती है।
2. कर्मचारी का स्वयं का अंशदान तथा उस पर अर्जित ब्याज/प्रतिफल की पूरी राशि आश्रित परिवार/नामिती को एकमुश्त नकद के रूप में प्रदान कर दी जाती है।
इसके साथ ही परिवार को सेवा उपदान (Death Gratuity) भी नियमों के तहत देय होता है। इसके विपरीत, यदि परिवार सीसीएस पारिवारिक पेंशन न चुनकर एनपीएस निकासी नियमों का विकल्प चुनता है, तभी संपूर्ण राशि (कर्मचारी + सरकार) एनपीएस वार्षिकी और एकमुश्त भुगतान हेतु प्रयुक्त होती है।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981, what is the maximum percentage of basic pension that a retiring government servant is legally permitted to commute?
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981, a government servant is entitled to commute for a lump-sum payment any fraction of their pension not exceeding forty percent (40%) of their basic monthly pension. Commutation provides immediate liquidity to the pensioner upon retirement by exchanging up to 40% of future monthly pension payments for an upfront capital sum. The remaining 60% of basic pension continues to be paid as the residual monthly pension. Importantly, Dearness Relief (DR) is always calculated on the full (100%) original basic pension, not on the reduced residual pension. The commuted amount is calculated using the official Commutation Table based on the age next birthday. The Head of Office (HOO) facilitates the commutation application through Form 1 or Form 1-A alongside pension papers on the Bhavishya platform.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 39 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (which incorporated the major reform introduced by the Department of Pension & Pensioners' Welfare in 2019 amending former Rule 38 of the 1972 Rules), the requirement of a minimum 10 years of qualifying service for grant of an Invalid Pension was done away with. Under the updated rules, an Invalid Pension is granted to a Government servant who retires from service on account of any bodily or mental infirmity which permanently incapacitates them for service, duly certified by a competent Medical Board, regardless of the length of qualifying service rendered. Even if the employee has rendered less than 10 years of service, they are entitled to an Invalid Pension calculated at 50% of the last basic pay / emoluments, subject to the conditions laid down in Rule 39. Prior to this amendment, government servants with less than 10 years of service received only an 'Invalid Gratuity'.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) No minimum service

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the updated Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, there is no minimum qualifying service requirement for granting an Invalid Pension. A government servant retired on medical grounds after being certified permanently incapacitated for further service by a duly constituted medical board is eligible for an invalid pension regardless of service length.

questions.question_english: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the statutory duties and responsibilities of the Head of Office (HoO) under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021:

questions.explanation_english: Statement D is completely incorrect. Under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 and established Supreme Court rulings, pension is recognized as a constitutional right to property under Article 300A, and the Head of Office has NO power or statutory authority to unilaterally withhold any percentage of a pensioner's monthly retirement pension for failure to vacate government residential accommodation. The statutory remedy available under Rules 67 and 68 relates strictly to Retirement Gratuity: the Directorate of Estates / Head of Office may withhold the full amount of Retirement Gratuity (or an amount equal to market license fee / damage rent) until the government quarter is vacated and a 'No Demand Certificate' (NDC) is issued. Statements A, B, and C are correct statutory duties of the HoO under Rules 53, 30, and 62/64.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन D पूर्णतः गलत है। सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 और न्यायिक निर्णयों के अनुसार, पेंशन संविधान के अनुच्छेद 300A के तहत संपत्ति का अधिकार है। कार्यालय प्रमुख (HoO) के पास सरकारी आवास खाली न करने के आधार पर मासिक पेंशन का 50% या कोई भी हिस्सा एकतरफा रोकने का कोई वैधानिक अधिकार नहीं है। नियम 67 और 68 के तहत केवल सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Retirement Gratuity) को आवास खाली होने तथा 'अदेयता प्रमाण पत्र' (No Demand Certificate) प्राप्त होने तक रोके रखने का प्रावधान है। कथन A (सेवानिवृत्ति से एक वर्ष पूर्व प्रक्रिया शुरू करना), B (18 वर्ष की सेवा या 5 वर्ष शेष रहने पर सत्यापन) तथा C (प्रशासनिक विलंब पर अनंतिम पेंशन) कार्यालय प्रमुख के सही वैधानिक कर्तव्य हैं।

questions.question_english: What is the fundamental financial difference between an ‘Advance’ from GPF and a ‘Withdrawal’ from GPF?
options_english: Advances must be repaid in monthly installments, while withdrawals are non-refundable.
Advances are interest-free, while withdrawals are charged interest.

questions.explanation_english:
Under the General Provident Fund (Central Services) Rules, 1960, the fundamental difference between a GPF Advance (Rule 12) and a GPF Withdrawal (Rule 15) lies in repayability:
1. GPF Advance: An advance is a temporary financial accommodation drawn from the subscriber's accumulated GPF balance. The sanctioned advance must be fully repaid into the subscriber's GPF account in equal monthly installments (generally between 12 and 24 installments, up to a maximum of 36 installments).
2. GPF Withdrawal: A withdrawal is a permanent, non-refundable withdrawal permitted after completing specified service milestones (such as 12 to 15 years of service or within 10 years of retirement). The subscriber is under no obligation to repay the withdrawn sum, and the amount permanently reduces the credit balance in the subscriber's GPF account.
Both can be sanctioned by the Head of Office / competent administrative authority for defined purposes. Hence, option A is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य भविष्य निधि (केंद्रीय सेवाएं) नियमावली, 1960 के अंतर्गत GPF अग्रिम (नियम 12) और GPF निकासी (नियम 15) के मध्य मुख्य वित्तीय अंतर उनकी वापसी-योग्यता (Repayability) में निहित है:
1. GPF अग्रिम (Advance): यह एक अस्थायी ऋण व्यवस्था है जिसकी निकासी अभिदाता अपने ही खाते से करता है। इस अग्रिम राशि को वेतन से 12 से 24 समान मासिक किस्तों (अधिकतम 36 किस्तों) में अनिवार्य रूप से वापस चुकाना (repay) होता है।
2. GPF निकासी (Withdrawal): यह एक स्थायी और गैर-वापसी योग्य (Non-refundable) आहरण है, जो एक निश्चित सेवा अवधि (जैसे 12 या 15 वर्ष की सेवा अथवा सेवानिवृत्ति से 10 वर्ष पूर्व) पूरी करने पर अनुमन्य होती है। इसे कभी भी वापस नहीं चुकाना पड़ता; यह राशि GPF खाते के शेष को स्थायी रूप से घटा देती है।
अतः सही विकल्प A है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Advances must be repaid in monthly installments, while withdrawals are non-refundable.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Under NPS rules, a government subscriber has the choice to defer the purchase of an annuity at the time of superannuation.
Reason (R): Deferment allows the subscriber to delay annuity purchase for up to 3 years from the date of retirement, providing flexibility to wait for more favourable market annuity rates.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Regulation 3 of the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, 2015:
1. Right of Annuity Deferment: An NPS subscriber retiring on superannuation is not legally obligated to purchase an annuity on the exact date of retirement. The rules provide the subscriber with the choice to defer the purchase of an annuity. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
2. Duration and Strategic Rationale: The subscriber can defer the purchase of an annuity for a maximum period of up to three (3) years from the date of retirement / superannuation. During this deferment period, the pension corpus remains invested in the subscriber's chosen pension funds under the PFRDA architecture, earning ongoing market returns. This provides valuable flexibility to retirees to time their purchase and lock in higher interest rates if prevailing annuity yields at the time of retirement are low. Hence, Reason (R) is true and accurately explains Assertion (A).
3. Additional Deferment: Subscribers also have the flexibility to defer the withdrawal of the 60% lump sum portion up to the age of 75 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
PFRDA (राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली के अंतर्गत निकास एवं आहरण) विनियम, 2015 के विनियम 3 के अनुसार:

2. आस्थगन की अवधि एवं औचित्य: अभिदाता सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि से अधिकतम 3 वर्ष की अवधि तक वार्षिकी खरीद को आस्थगित कर सकता है। इस अवधि के दौरान उसकी पेंशन निधि बाजार में निवेशित रहकर वृद्धि करती रहती है और अभिदाता को सेवानिवृत्ति के समय प्रतिकूल ब्याज दरों से बचने तथा भविष्य में उच्च ब्याज/वार्षिकी दरों का लाभ उठाने का लचीलापन मिलता है। अतः कारण (R) सत्य है और अभिकथन (A) का सही स्पष्टीकरण है।
3. एकमुश्त राशि का आस्थगन: इसके अतिरिक्त, अभिदाता 60% एकमुश्त कॉर्पस की निकासी को भी 75 वर्ष की आयु तक आस्थगित कर सकता है। अतः A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 80CCD(1B) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, what is the maximum additional tax deduction permissible exclusively for individual contributions made to an NPS Tier I account, over and above the Section 80C threshold?
questions.explanation_english:
To incentivize long-term retirement planning through the National Pension System, the Finance Act, 2015 introduced Section 80CCD(1B) in the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Tax Provisions Governing NPS Tier I:
1. Section 80CCD(1): Allows deduction for employee's own contribution towards NPS Tier I up to 10% of salary (Basic Pay + DA). However, this deduction is subject to the overall ceiling limit of ₹1,50,000 under Section 80CCE (which bundles Section 80C, 80CCC, and 80CCD(1)).
2. Section 80CCD(1B): Provides an exclusive additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 for individual contributions deposited into the NPS Tier I account. This deduction is specifically over and above the ₹1,50,000 limit of Section 80CCE, allowing a total tax deduction of up to ₹2,00,000 for salaried employees under the old tax regime.
3. Tier II Ineligibility: This ₹50,000 exclusive benefit under Section 80CCD(1B) is not available for deposits made into standard Tier II accounts.
4. Section 80CCD(2): The employer's contribution (up to 14% of Basic + DA for Central Government employees) is separately deductible under Section 80CCD(2) without being restricted by the ₹1.5 lakh or ₹50,000 limits (subject to the aggregate ₹7.5 lakh annual ceiling across NPS, EPF, and superannuation funds under Section 17(2)(vii)).

राष्ट्रीय पेंशन प्रणाली के माध्यम से दीर्घकालिक सेवानिवृत्ति बचत को प्रोत्साहित करने के लिए, वित्त अधिनियम, 2015 द्वारा आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 में धारा 80CCD(1B) जोड़ी गई थी।

NPS टियर I से संबंधित आयकर प्रावधान:
1. धारा 80CCD(1): कर्मचारी द्वारा अपने वेतन (मूल वेतन + DA) के 10% तक के NPS टियर I अंशदान पर कर कटौती की अनुमति देती है। हालांकि, यह कटौती धारा 80CCE के तहत निर्धारित ₹1,50,000 की कुल सीमा (धारा 80C, 80CCC और 80CCD(1) को मिलाकर) के अधीन होती है।
2. धारा 80CCD(1B): NPS टियर I खाते में जमा किए गए व्यक्तिगत अंशदान के लिए विशेष रूप से ₹50,000 तक की अतिरिक्त कर कटौती प्रदान करती है। यह कटौती धारा 80CCE की ₹1,50,000 की सीमा से अलग और अतिरिक्त है, जिससे पुरानी कर व्यवस्था के तहत कुल ₹2,00,000 तक की कर छूट प्राप्त की जा सकती है।

4. धारा 80CCD(2): केंद्र सरकार के कर्मचारियों के लिए नियोक्ता (सरकार) द्वारा किया जाने वाला 14% तक का अंशदान धारा 80CCD(2) के तहत अलग से कर-मुक्त होता है, जो ₹1.5 लाख या ₹50,000 की सीमा से स्वतंत्र होता है।

Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Upon exiting the National Pension System (NPS) on superannuation, it is legally mandatory for a subscriber to utilize at least 40% of their accumulated pension wealth to purchase an annuity from an Annuity Service Provider (ASP) empanelled by PFRDA.
Reason (R): The mandatory annuitization requirement ensures that the retiree receives a regular, guaranteed monthly income stream throughout post-retirement life, thereby fulfilling the fundamental social security objective of a defined contribution pension system.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Under the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, 2015:
- Assertion (A) is TRUE: Upon normal superannuation at age 60 (or the statutory age of retirement), a subscriber is legally mandated to utilize a minimum of 40% of their accumulated pension wealth in the PRAN to purchase a life annuity from an Annuity Service Provider (ASP) empanelled with PFRDA. Up to 60% can be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum (or 100% lump sum if the total corpus is up to ₹5 lakh).
- Reason (R) is TRUE: The fundamental social security purpose behind mandating annuity purchase is to protect the retiree from longevity risk and investment market volatility by guaranteeing an uninterrupted, predictable monthly pension stream till death (with annuity variants offering spouse continuation or return of purchase price).
Since Reason (R) provides the direct institutional rationale for why Assertion (A) is mandated, both statements are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.question_english: Under Rule 31 and Rule 45 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, when determining 'Emoluments' for the calculation of Death Gratuity in the case of a government servant who died while on authorized leave with allowances, which pay is taken into account?
options_english: The actual leave salary drawn by the employee on the date of death.
The minimum basic pay of the applicable pay level in the Pay Matrix.
Only the basic pay without any consideration of Dearness Allowance during leave.
The pay that the government servant would have drawn had they been actively on duty.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 31 and Rule 45 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021:
1. **Emoluments for Gratuity:** Emoluments for the purpose of retirement or death gratuity include basic pay in the Pay Matrix level plus the Dearness Allowance admissible on the date of cessation of service / demise.
2. **Death while on Leave with Allowances:** If a government servant dies while on authorized leave with leave salary (such as Earned Leave, Half Pay Leave, or Commuted Leave), the emoluments for calculating Death Gratuity shall be the pay that the employee would have drawn had they been on duty on that date, and NOT the reduced leave salary (e.g., half pay salary).
3. **Protection of Family:** This protective statutory provision ensures that a bereaved family is not financially penalized simply because the deceased employee was compelled to be on medical leave or half-pay leave prior to their demise.
4. **DDO Responsibility:** In Form 7 and Bhavishya filings, the DDO/Head of Office certifies notional duty pay for emolument assessment in such bereavement cases.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 31 तथा नियम 45 के अनुसार:
1. **उपदान हेतु परिलब्धियां:** उपदान (Gratuity) की गणना के लिए परिलब्धियों में संबंधित पे मैट्रिक्स लेवल में मूल वेतन तथा उस तिथि पर लागू महंगाई भत्ता (DA) शामिल होता है।
2. **अवकाश के दौरान मृत्यु पर नियम:** यदि किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी की मृत्यु वेतन सहित अवकाश (जैसे अर्जित अवकाश या अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश) के दौरान होती है, तो मृत्यु उपदान की गणना के लिए 'परिलब्धियों' का निर्धारण उस वेतन के आधार पर किया जाता है जो वह आहरित करता यदि वह अवकाश के स्थान पर सक्रिय रूप से कर्तव्य (Duty) पर उपस्थित होता।
3. **परिवार का वित्तीय संरक्षण:** यह नियम यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि अंतिम समय में गंभीर बीमारी के कारण अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश (Half Pay Leave) पर रहने की स्थिति में शोकाकुल परिवार को ग्रेच्युटी की गणना में कोई वित्तीय नुकसान न उठाना पड़े।
4. **कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) का दायित्व:** कार्यालय प्रमुख और DDO 'भविष्य' पोर्टल पर फॉर्म 7 भरते समय इस काल्पनिक कर्तव्य वेतन (Notional duty pay) को आधार बनाकर ही उपदान की गणना प्रमाणित करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The pay they would have drawn had they been on duty.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When calculating emoluments for Death Gratuity in the case of a government servant who dies while on authorized leave with leave salary, the pay considered is the basic pay the employee would have drawn had they been actively on duty instead of being on leave on the date of demise.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 43 of CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021 (earlier Rule 48-A of CCS Pension Rules 1972), a government servant who has completed 20 years of qualifying service may take voluntary retirement by giving three months' notice in writing to the appointing authority. Following the implementation of the 6th Central Pay Commission recommendations (effective 01.01.2006), the requirement of 33 years of qualifying service for full pension was delinked. A government servant who has completed the minimum qualifying service of 10 years is entitled to full pension calculated at 50% of the last basic pay drawn or 50% of average emoluments, whichever is higher. No pro-rata reduction or penalty is imposed for retiring before the age of 60. Furthermore, the earlier provision of adding up to 5 years of notional weightage was repealed with effect from 01.01.2006.

1. Minimum Service Threshold: The minimum qualifying service required to become eligible for any pension under UPS is 10 years (consistent with CCS Pension Rules).
2. Assured Minimum Pension: Employees who retire on superannuation after completing at least 10 years of qualifying service are assured a minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month. (Note: Under the Old Pension Scheme/CCS Pension Rules, 2021, the minimum pension is ₹9,000 per month; under UPS, it has been established at ₹10,000 per month).
3. Social Security: This safeguard ensures that employees joining late in government service or retiring with shorter tenures (10 to 25 years) do not receive an unviable or sub-standard pension payout.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 10(2) of the Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021, every Government servant covered under NPS is required, at the time of joining service, to exercise an option in Form 1 indicating whether they wish to be covered under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules or under the National Pension System in the event of death in harness or retirement on medical invalidation/disablement.
The statutory rules clearly prescribe that if a government servant fails to exercise this option, the default option for the first fifteen (15) years of service shall be the benefits under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules (i.e., Family Pension or Invalid Pension). After the completion of 15 years of service, if no option has been exercised, the default entitlement automatically switches to the benefits admissible under the National Pension System regulations.

questions.question_english: An NPS subscriber can make a partial withdrawal from their Tier-I account for the treatment of specified critical illnesses. Which of the following is NOT classified as a permissible reason under the specified statutory list?
options_english: Routine Cataract surgery
Cancer
Kidney Failure (End Stage Renal Failure)
Major Organ Transplant
questions.explanation_english:
Under Regulation 8 of the PFRDA (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations:
1. **Partial Withdrawal Facility:** A subscriber who has contributed to NPS for at least three years may withdraw up to 25% of their own accumulated contributions (excluding employer's contribution and accrued returns) for specified purposes, up to a maximum of three times during the entire tenure.
2. **Statutory Critical Illnesses:** Permitted critical illnesses for medical treatment of self, spouse, children, or dependent parents include:
   - Cancer
   - Kidney Failure (End Stage Renal Failure)
   - Major Organ Transplant (heart, kidney, liver, lung, pancreas, bone marrow)
   - Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (CABG)
   - Stroke, Coma, Multiple Sclerosis, Blindness, Paralysis, and COVID-19.
3. **Exclusion of Elective Surgeries:** Routine elective minor surgeries, such as uncomplicated cataract surgery, do not constitute a critical/life-threatening illness under PFRDA regulations and are not permissible grounds for partial withdrawal from the Tier-I pension corpus.

1. **आंशिक आहरण की सुविधा:** कम से कम तीन वर्ष तक NPS में अंशदान करने वाला अभिदाता अपने स्वयं के अंशदान के अधिकतम 25% तक का आंशिक आहरण विनिर्दिष्ट कारणों से (संपूर्ण सेवाकाल में अधिकतम तीन बार) कर सकता है।
2. **विनिर्दिष्ट गंभीर बीमारियां:** स्वयं, पति/पत्नी, बच्चों या आश्रित माता-पिता के उपचार के लिए अनुमत बीमारियों में कैंसर, गुर्दे की विफलता (एंड-स्टेज रीनल फेल्योर), प्रमुख अंग प्रत्यारोपण (हृदय, गुर्दा, यकृत, फेफड़े आदि), कोरोनरी आर्टरी बाईपास ग्राफ्ट (CABG), स्ट्रोक, कोमा और कोविड-19 आदि शामिल हैं।
3. **सामान्य सर्जरी का अपवर्जन:** सामान्य एवं नियमित ऐच्छिक सर्जरी जैसे मोतियाबिंद की सर्जरी (Cataract surgery) इस गंभीर जीवन-घातक बीमारियों की सूची में शामिल नहीं है; अतः इसके लिए टियर-I से आंशिक आहरण की अनुमति नहीं दी जा सकती।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Routine Cataract surgery

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under PFRDA regulations, partial withdrawal from NPS Tier I is permitted for treating specified critical illnesses, including cancer, end-stage renal failure, major organ transplants, and heart surgeries. Routine elective medical procedures, such as uncomplicated cataract surgery, are not classified under the statutory list of critical illnesses for partial withdrawal.

questions.question_english:
A Head of Office (HoO) realizes that a retiring teacher failed to fill the required pension forms on time due to severe illness. The HoO issues a Provisional Pension to avoid financial hardship. 

For what maximum period can the HoO sanction this provisional pension initially?
options_english: Three months
Six months
Nine months
Twelve months
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 62 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021 (corresponding to Rule 64 of the 1972 Rules), the statutory procedure for sanctioning provisional pension and provisional gratuity is designed to prevent financial hardship to a retiring government servant when pension papers cannot be processed or verified in time before retirement.

Key administrative mandates for the Head of Office (HoO) include:
1. Where the pension papers cannot be finalized on time—whether due to delayed submission by the employee (e.g., severe illness) or administrative delays in verifying the service book—the Head of Office is duty-bound to assess and sanction a Provisional Pension and Provisional Retirement Gratuity.
2. The Head of Office can sanction this provisional pension initially for a period not exceeding six months from the date following the date of retirement.
3. The amount of provisional pension cannot exceed the maximum pension admissible on the basis of the qualifying service verified up to that date.
4. If the final Pension Payment Order (PPO) is not issued within these six months, the Accounts Officer may, on request, extend the provisional pension or issue the final authorization.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 62 (पूर्ववर्ती 1972 नियमों के नियम 64) के अनुसार, यदि किसी सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले सरकारी कर्मचारी के पेंशन दस्तावेज समय पर तैयार या सत्यापित नहीं हो पाते हैं—चाहे वह कर्मचारी की गंभीर बीमारी के कारण प्रपत्र जमा करने में देरी हो या सेवा पुस्तिका के सत्यापन में प्रशासनिक विलंब—तो कार्यालयाध्यक्ष (HoO) को उसे वित्तीय कठिनाई से बचाने के लिए अनंतिम पेंशन (Provisional Pension) और अनंतिम उपदान (Provisional Gratuity) स्वीकृत करने का अधिकार है।

इस संबंध में वैधानिक प्रावधान निम्नलिखित हैं:
1. कार्यालयाध्यक्ष द्वारा यह अनंतिम पेंशन प्रारंभिक रूप से सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि के अगले दिन से अधिकतम छह महीने (6 months) की अवधि के लिए स्वीकृत की जा सकती है।
2. अनंतिम पेंशन की राशि उस समय तक सत्यापित अर्हक सेवा के आधार पर अनुमेय अधिकतम पेंशन से अधिक नहीं होगी।
3. यदि छह महीने की इस अवधि के भीतर अंतिम पेंशन भुगतान आदेश (PPO) जारी नहीं हो पाता है, तो कार्यालयाध्यक्ष वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) को मामले से अवगत कराकर इसके विस्तार अथवा अंतिम निपटान का अनुरोध करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Six months

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021, if pension processing is delayed, the Head of Office is empowered to sanction a provisional pension to the retiring government servant. This provisional pension can be sanctioned initially for a maximum period not exceeding six months while final pension papers are processed.

questions.question_english: A government school teacher draws a monthly Basic Pay of ₹60,000, and the Dearness Allowance (DA) is 50%. What is the teacher's own mandatory monthly deduction towards the NPS Tier I account?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Implementation of National Pension System) Rules, 2021, an employee's mandatory monthly contribution to the NPS Tier I account is fixed at 10% of their Emoluments (Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance).

Step-by-Step Calculation:
1. Monthly Basic Pay = ₹60,000.
2. Dearness Allowance (DA) rate = 50% of Basic Pay.
   DA Amount = 50% of ₹60,000 = ₹30,000.
3. Total Emoluments for NPS Calculation = Basic Pay + DA = ₹60,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹90,000.
4. Employee's Mandatory Deduction (10%) = 10% of ₹90,000 = ₹9,000.

Additional Context for DDOs / School Heads:
- The government's matching monthly contribution (14% under Rule 6) on the same emoluments would be: 14% of ₹90,000 = ₹12,600 (represented by Option D).
- Total monthly credit into the teacher's PRAN = ₹9,000 (Employee) + ₹12,600 (Government) = ₹21,600.
- However, since the question specifically asks for the teacher's own mandatory deduction, the correct figure is ₹9,000.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (NPS का क्रियान्वयन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 5 के अनुसार, NPS टियर I खाते में कर्मचारी का मासिक अनिवार्य अंशदान उसकी उपलब्धियों (मूल वेतन + महंगाई भत्ता) का 10% होता है।

चरणबद्ध गणना:
1. मासिक मूल वेतन = ₹60,000
2. महंगाई भत्ता (DA) की दर = 50%
   DA की राशि = ₹60,000 का 50% = ₹30,000
3. NPS गणना हेतु कुल उपलब्धियां = मूल वेतन + DA = ₹60,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹90,000
4. कर्मचारी का स्वयं का अनिवार्य अंशदान (10%) = ₹90,000 का 10% = ₹9,000

DDO / विद्यालय प्राचार्यों के लिए अतिरिक्त जानकारी:
- सरकार द्वारा दिया जाने वाला 14% का समतुल्य नियोक्ता अंशदान = ₹90,000 का 14% = ₹12,600 (विकल्प D)।
- शिक्षक के प्रान (PRAN) खाते में प्रति माह कुल जमा राशि = ₹9,000 (कर्मचारी) + ₹12,600 (सरकार) = ₹21,600 होगी।
- चूंकि प्रश्न में केवल शिक्षक के स्वयं के मासिक अंशदान (वेतन कटौती) के बारे में पूछा गया है, अतः सही उत्तर ₹9,000 है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) ₹9,000

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: An employee’s mandatory monthly deduction for the NPS Tier I account is ten percent of basic pay plus dearness allowance. With a basic pay of sixty thousand rupees and dearness allowance at fifty percent (thirty thousand rupees), total emoluments equal ninety thousand rupees. Ten percent of ninety thousand rupees yields a monthly deduction of nine thousand rupees.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statutory forms is used by the Head of Office (HOO) to assess, calculate, and authorize the pension and retirement gratuity of a retiring government servant under the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021?
options_english: Form 3
Form 7
Form 14
Form 16
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 57 and Rule 59 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021:
1. **Statutory Role of Form 7:** **Form 7** is the definitive official form prescribed for the Head of Office (HOO) to assess, process, and formally calculate the pension and retirement gratuity admissible to a retiring government servant.
2. **Contents of Form 7:** It includes detailed records of:
   - Verification of qualifying service and periods of non-qualifying service (dies-non, unauthorized absence, extraordinary leave without medical certificate).
   - Computation of emoluments and average emoluments over the last 10 months.
   - Calculated amount of superannuation pension and retirement gratuity.
   - Recoverable government dues (license fees, advances, etc.).
3. **Bhavishya Portal Integration:** In the Bhavishya electronic workflow, Form 7 is digitally populated and verified by the HOO before transmission to the Pay and Accounts Officer (PAO) four months prior to the retirement date.
4. **Other Forms:**
   - **Form 3:** Details of family submitted by the employee.
   - **Form 6:** Formal application for pension submitted by the retiring employee.
   - **Form 14:** Application for family pension on death of a pensioner/employee.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 57 और 59 के अनुसार:
1. **फॉर्म 7 की वैधानिक भूमिका:** **फॉर्म 7** वह आधिकारिक प्रपत्र है जिसका उपयोग कार्यालय प्रमुख (Head of Office - HOO) द्वारा सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले सरकारी कर्मचारी की पेंशन तथा सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान के निर्धारण, मूल्यांकन और प्राधिकार हेतु किया जाता है।
2. **फॉर्म 7 की मुख्य विषय-वस्तु:** इसमें निम्नलिखित विवरण दर्ज होते हैं:
   - सेवा पुस्तिका के आधार पर अर्हक सेवा का पूर्ण सत्यापन तथा गैर-अर्हक सेवा का विवरण।
   - अंतिम 10 महीनों की परिलब्धियों और औसत परिलब्धियों की गणना।
   - स्वीकार्य पेंशन, उपदान और पेंशन रूपांतरण की सटीक गणना।
   - सरकारी देय राशियों (मकान किराया/लाइसेंस शुल्क, अग्रिम आदि) का समायोजन।
3. **'भविष्य' पोर्टल पर प्रक्रिया:** 'भविष्य' (Bhavishya) पोर्टल पर HOO द्वारा सेवानिवृत्ति की तिथि से 4 महीने पूर्व फॉर्म 7 को डिजिटल रूप से सत्यापित कर वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) को प्रेषित किया जाता है।
4. **अन्य फॉर्म:**
   - **फॉर्म 3:** सरकारी सेवक द्वारा परिवार के सदस्यों का विवरण।
   - **फॉर्म 6:** कर्मचारी द्वारा स्वयं की पेंशन हेतु आवेदन।
   - **फॉर्म 14:** कर्मचारी/पेंशनभोगी के निधन पर पारिवारिक पेंशन हेतु आवेदन।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Form 7

questions.question_english: What is the prescribed maximum ceiling limit for a standard monthly retirement pension that can be sanctioned to a government servant under OPS as per the 7th CPC guidelines?
options_english: ₹1,00,000 per month
₹1,25,000 per month
₹1,50,000 per month
₹2,50,000 per month
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 44 of the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, and the 7th Central Pay Commission guidelines, the maximum monthly pension permissible is fixed at 50% of the highest pay in the Government of India. The maximum basic pay under the 7th CPC Pay Matrix is ₹2,50,000 per month (drawn by the Cabinet Secretary of India and officers of equivalent rank in Level 17 - Apex Pay Scale). Consequently, 50% of this maximum pay establishes the statutory upper ceiling for monthly pension at ₹1,25,000 per month (plus applicable Dearness Relief).
questions.explanation_hindi: सीसीएस (पेंशन) नियम, 2021 के नियम 44 तथा 7वें वेतन आयोग के दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार, मासिक पेंशन की अधिकतम सीमा भारत सरकार में उच्चतम मूल वेतन के 50% पर निर्धारित की गई है। 7वें वेतन आयोग में उच्चतम मूल वेतन ₹2,50,000 प्रति माह (स्तर 17 - कैबिनेट सचिव व समकक्ष) है। अतः इसका 50% यानी ₹1,25,000 प्रति माह पेंशन की अधिकतम वैधानिक सीमा (अधिकतम सीमा / ceiling limit) है, जिस पर नियमानुसार महंगाई राहत (DR) देय होती है।
